Container.Name: manabrew-relay
Container.Overview: Manabrew relay (manabrew-server): lobbies, matchmaking and message relay. Browser and desktop clients, and the optional Forge node, all connect to it. It never runs games itself. Speaks plain ws:// on 9443; put it behind a TLS reverse proxy on its own hostname (e.g. relay.example.com) so clients connect over wss:// on 443.
Container.Requires: Put this, manabrew-web and manabrew-node on the same user-defined Docker network (default: manabrew). Create it once with: docker network create manabrew

Config.Name: WebSocket port
Config.Description: Lobby/game WebSocket (plain ws://). Point your reverse proxy's relay hostname here. Don't port-forward this directly unless you accept unencrypted traffic.

Config.Name: Health port
Config.Description: HTTP /health endpoint, for monitoring only. Never needs to be public.

Config.Name: Server key
Config.Description: Shared key every client and node must present as the first message, or the relay drops the connection (no room list, no room creation without it). This is your access control: use a long random value (openssl rand -hex 32), give it only to friends, and keep it OUT of manabrew-web's RELAY_PASSWORD unless that site is behind a login. Must match SELF_HOSTED_NODE_SERVER_KEY on manabrew-node. Falls back to 'forge' if empty - never leave it empty.

Config.Name: Max rooms
Config.Description: Maximum concurrent rooms on this relay.

Config.Name: Bind address
Config.Description: Address the relay binds inside the container.

Config.Name: LAN mDNS advertise
Config.Description: Answer mDNS so desktop clients on your LAN auto-discover this relay. Only works with Network=host or br0 (mDNS doesn't cross Docker bridges). If true and Server key is empty, the key becomes 'manabrew-lan'. Leave false for internet play.
